prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 服务器安全基线核查记录 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 8 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "受检服务器唯一编号" · longest unbreakable word 20px · one-line width 138px
  col 2: header "系统账户口令强度" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 3: header "外部网络访问开放" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 4: header "日志留存天数达标" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 123px
  col 5: header "漏洞补丁更新状态" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 6: header "高危端口关闭数量" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 7: header "近三十天告警次数" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 8: header "应急联系人确认情况" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 138px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A zh-CN server security-baseline audit record: one row per server, one column per control or measure, used to verify compliance and compare servers.","reading":"Readers identify a server in column 1, then scan across its row for pass/fail and counts; auditors also scan down individual check columns to compare servers. Headers are long and can wrap, while row IDs and values are short and must remain stable.","groups":["col 1 — server identity / row header; it should stand apart from the checks","cols 2, 3, 5, 8 — binary compliance or confirmation checks (是/否); same visual role","cols 4, 6, 7 — quantitative measures (days, port count, alert count); short numeric values"],"keep_intact":["server IDs 01–06","是/否 status values","numeric values such as 180, 365, 30, and port/alert counts","numbers and identifiers must not break across lines"],"may_wrap":["Chinese header labels in every column, especially 受检服务器唯一编号 and 应急联系人确认情况","header text may wrap at character boundaries; no data cell needs wrapping"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[110,85,85,85,85,85,85,99],"idea":"Balanced grid: near-equal interior check columns with slightly wider row-ID and contact columns so every header wraps cleanly to two lines."},{"name":"B","widths":[96,100,100,81,99,81,81,81],"idea":"Status-first: spend width on the four binary checks, keep the three numeric measures at the two-line minimum, and use a compact row-ID column."},{"name":"C","widths":[130,81,81,81,81,81,81,103],"idea":"Bookend-heavy: make server ID and contact the widest columns while all six check columns sit at the practical two-line minimum."}]}
